title: Endpoint Resilience Charter: measurable SLIs, staged regional evacuation, and token-aware shedding
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: establish a repeatable, per-endpoint SLI/SLO declaration and an operational policy for error budget burn, progressive circuit breaking, and cross-region evacuation that is sensitive to KV cache and token footprint. This ticket scopes the charter, measurement definitions, failover thresholds, and the automation rules we will instrument in Prometheus/Alertmanager + Grafana + the control plane.

Context and motivation:
- Increasing multi-region traffic means we must reason about capacity and quality per endpoint/model variant rather than at service granularity.
- Many outages to date are from sudden tail-latency regressions and cache-unfriendly routes; current global circuit responses are too coarse and cause unnecessary failovers.
- Customers expect predictable degradation paths and clear guarantees; we require per-endpoint declarations so the Console and runbooks can present concise contracts.

Scope (what this ticket will produce):
1) Canonical SLI definitions (strings):
   - success_rate: fraction of requests returning 2xx within request-accept window. Measured as count(2xx) / count(total) over rolling 5m.
   - latency_p95_ms: 95th percentile server-to-client latency excluding client-side stream delays. Window: 5m.
   - quality_eval_pass: fraction of sampled responses passing an auto-eval prompt set tied to the route (daily sampling target: 1k responses).
   - token_overrun_ratio: fraction of requests where token consumption exceeded the route's historical 99th percentile (used to detect cost/rate anomalies).
   - kv_cache_hit_rate: request-level boolean if prefix/KV cache was used; aggregated as a rate.

2) SLO targets and error budgets (strings):
   - Tiered defaults: P0/P1/P2 routes mapped to targets "99.95% success_rate monthly" (P0), "99.9%" (P1), "99.5%" (P2); latency_p95 targets: P0 < 200ms, P1 < 400ms, P2 < 800ms.
   - quality_eval_pass baseline: P0 >= 98% pass on canary promptset, P1 >= 95%.
   - Error budget windows: rolling 30d and monthly aligned calendar windows.

3) Automated burn detection and staged response (strings):
   - Burn thresholds: warn at 25% budget used in 30d, elevated at 50%, critical at 80%.
   - Actions at warn: PM/owner Slack notification and chart pinned to on-call dashboard.
   - Actions at elevated: throttle non-critical background jobs, suspend non-essential long-running batch requests for the tenant class consuming the budget.
   - Actions at critical: trigger the circuit-breaker choreography (see below).

4) Progressive circuit-breaker choreography (strings):
   - Phase 0 (soft degrade): reduce per-request max tokens by 20% for non-P0 tenants, enable structured truncation templates.
   - Phase 1 (variant fallback): route requests to cheaper/quantized model variant with documented quality delta; use A/B fallback with 10% traffic shift first.
   - Phase 2 (regional ejection): temporarily eject region from read/write serving for non-pinned customers and route to standby region with KV-cache warmup protocol.
   - Phase 3 (evacuation): full flow-level admission control, <= 5% of requests allowed for low-priority tenants; preserve P0 contractual traffic where capacity allows.

5) Load-shedding primitives and tenant prioritization (strings):
   - Token-aware shedding: tenant queue priority is token-weighted (token_cost = tokens_requested * tenant_weight_multiplier). This prevents small high-priority requests from being blocked by long generative requests.
   - KV-cache-aware eviction: requests that would miss KV cache are deprioritized during elevated burn since they cost more CPU per token.
   - Grace windows: short-lived short-circuit for conversational routes that have active session slots (session-aware token reservations).

6) Observability and runbooks (strings):
   - Dashboards: grafana.redwood.internal/d/endpoint-resilience (canary SLI, burn rate, regional capacity, kv-hit heatmap).
   - Alerts: Prometheus rules with automatic PagerDuty escalation for critical burn.
   - Runbooks: confluence.redwood.ai/pages/Endpoint+Resilience+Runbook (links to rollback steps, runbooks for phased circuit stages, checklist for manual KV cache pre-warm).

Design trade-offs and decisions to record (strings):
- Why per-endpoint SLIs? Coarse service-level SLOs mask noisy routes and make fair crediting/imposition of throttles difficult.
- Why token-aware shedding? Token footprint correlates strongly with GPU time; treating requests equally yields poor utility.
- Why staged evacuation vs immediate region failover? Staged reduces blast radius and allows cache-dependent warmups to succeed, avoiding thrashing.

Implementation plan (milestones as strings):
- M1 (2w): finalize SLI definitions, implement Prometheus metrics and sampling hooks for quality_eval_pass.
- M2 (3w): implement burn-rate rules, hook Alertmanager -> PagerDuty, build Grafana dashboard initial version.
- M3 (3w): implement soft-degrade and variant-fallback automation in control plane (feature-flagged).
- M4 (4w): implement token-aware queueing + KV-cache-aware prioritizer in runtime scheduler; dry-run with synthetic traffic.
- M5 (2w): run multi-region chaos exercise and validate runbooks; iterate on thresholds.

Acceptance criteria (strings):
- Documented SLI definitions and targets are published in Confluence.
- Prometheus metrics emit required metrics for 95% of endpoints.
- Automation can trigger Phase 0/1 without human intervention behind feature flag; manual escalation for Phase 2/3.
- Chaos run shows improved graceful degradation (less than 2x increase in P0 error budget burn rate vs baseline).

Risks and mitigation (strings):
- Risk: false positives from noisy eval sampling can cause unnecessary failovers. Mitigation: require rolling-window smoothing + holdout checks before critical actions.
- Risk: variant fallback may regress quality unexpectedly. Mitigation: canary at 10% then 50% with continuous quality_eval_pass checks and automated rollback.

Deliverables and links (strings):
- RFC/Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Endpoint+Resilience+Charter
- Grafana dashboard (prototype): https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/endpoint-resilience
- Control-plane PR for staged fallback: https://github.com/redwood-inference/control-plane/pull/8421
- Quality eval harness (repo): https://github.com/redwood-inference/evals/tree/endpoint-resilience

Notes for reviewers (strings):
- Focus review on SLI definitions (are we measuring the user-perceived dimensions?) and the proposed automation safety gates.
- Ops: please validate the Grafana panels and alert severity mapping.
